name: Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms (RJSC)
service: Name clearance; registration of companies, partnerships, societies and trade organisations; annual and change-return filing; and certified copies.
process: Submit applications and returns through the RJSC online application, using the published process guides, forms and fee schedule for the entity type.
applicationPath: Create an account at app.roc.gov.bd, obtain name clearance where required, then file the registration documents and later statutory returns.
notes: RJSC creates and maintains the legal record for registered entities; it does not issue a trade licence or protect a trademark. Name clearance is required before registering most new entities, while RJSC's process guide exempts foreign companies and partnership firms from that step.

name: BIDA One Stop Service
service: Registration and approval of domestic, foreign and joint-venture industrial projects, branch or liaison offices, foreign-worker services and other investor-facing permits.
process: Submit documents, pay applicable charges, track applications and download approvals through the BIDA OSS portal; requests are routed to BIDA or an integrated agency.
applicationPath: Create an organisation account on bidaquickserv.org and choose the specific BIDA or partner-agency service you need.
notes: BIDA is the principal agency for private investment promotion and facilitation, and OSS brings many investor approvals into one account. It is particularly relevant to industrial projects, foreign investment, foreign staff and branch or liaison offices, but it does not replace RJSC registration or every sector licence.

name: National Board of Revenue – e-TIN and income tax
service: Electronic Taxpayer Identification Number registration and income-tax return preparation, payment and filing.
process: Register or manage a TIN at incometax.gov.bd, then use the separate e-Return system at etaxnbr.gov.bd to file applicable returns.
ministry: Internal Resources Division, Ministry of Finance
applicationPath: Obtain an e-TIN at incometax.gov.bd/TINHome. For e-Return registration, individuals need an existing TIN and a mobile number registered biometrically against their NID.
notes: An e-TIN is the taxpayer identifier; e-Return is the separate service used to prepare, pay and submit income-tax returns. A TIN is not company registration and does not by itself show that a taxpayer's filing obligations are up to date.

name: National Board of Revenue – VAT Online (BIN)
service: VAT registration or turnover-tax enlistment, Business Identification Number issuance and Mushak return filing.
process: Create a VAT Online account, submit the applicable Mushak registration or enlistment form and use the same system for returns.
ministry: Internal Resources Division, Ministry of Finance
applicationPath: Create an account at vat.gov.bd and submit Mushak 2.1 for registration or enlistment; determine which status applies before filing.
notes: A BIN identifies a person in the VAT system; VAT registration and turnover-tax enlistment are different statuses with different thresholds and return obligations. Applicability also depends on the activity, so do not treat a BIN as a generic business-registration certificate.

name: Dhaka North City Corporation – trade licence
service: Trade licence issue and annual renewal for businesses inside the DNCC area.
process: Apply through DNCC's e-Revenue portal, upload the required identity, premises and business documents, then pay after approval; some business categories require additional review.
applicationPath: Create an account at erevenue.dncc.gov.bd/cp/cportal/cp/northcc.aspx for a new licence or renewal and follow the document checklist shown for the business category.
notes: DNCC issues the annual trade licence for establishments located inside Dhaka North. The fee and supporting clearances depend on the stated trade and premises, so the licence should match the actual business address and activity.

name: Dhaka South City Corporation – trade licence
service: Trade licence issue and annual renewal for businesses inside the DSCC area.
process: Submit the application through the DSCC e-Revenue portal; the prescribed form and premises, identity and company documents are reviewed, with field verification before issue where required.
applicationPath: Use erevenue.dscc.gov.bd/cp/cportal/cp/southcc.aspx and follow DSCC's issue or renewal procedure for your business type.
notes: DSCC issues the annual trade licence for establishments located inside Dhaka South. Businesses elsewhere must use their own city corporation, municipality or other competent local authority rather than this portal.

name: Chief Controller of Imports and Exports (CCIE)
service: Import Registration Certificate and Export Registration Certificate issue, renewal and amendment, plus related import and export permissions.
process: Apply and manage certificates through CCIE's Online Licensing Module, which uses mobile OTP verification and service-specific supporting documents.
applicationPath: Create an account at olm.ccie.gov.bd, choose the relevant IRC, ERC or permit service and follow the current document and renewal requirements.
notes: CCIE is the licensing authority for businesses carrying out regulated commercial import and export activity. Choose the correct certificate class for the activity and confirm its supporting documents before committing to a shipment or contract.

name: Export Promotion Bureau (EPB)
service: Exporter promotion, market intelligence, trade-fair support, export statistics, exporter profiles and access to export-related certification services.
process: Use the service-specific portals linked by EPB, including the Exporter Database and Bangladesh Single Window for applicable certificates of origin.
applicationPath: Choose the relevant e-service from epb.gov.bd; exporters can create a profile at edb.epb.gov.bd, while origin-certificate applications use the Bangladesh Single Window.
notes: EPB helps active or prospective exporters find markets, participate in promotion programmes and use export-service systems. It does not issue the IRC or ERC required for the underlying trading activity; those certificates come from CCIE.

name: Department of Environment (DOE)
service: Environmental Clearance Certificate issue and renewal, with requirements based on the project's activity and environmental category.
process: Register in the Department of Environment's ECC system, complete the applicable forms, upload supporting documents and pay system-generated fees online or by challan.
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
applicationPath: Create an account at ecc-beta.doe.gov.bd, identify the correct project category and follow the online new-application or renewal workflow.
notes: The environmental category determines the studies, clearances and supporting documents a project needs. Check the actual activity and premises against the current rules before starting operations rather than assuming the business is exempt from its sector label alone.

name: Department of Patents, Designs and Trademarks (DPDT)
service: Trademark, patent, industrial-design and geographical-indication registration and publication.
process: Use the relevant DPDT application process, forms, checklist and fee schedule; electronic filing is provided through the Bangladesh WIPO filing dashboard.
applicationPath: Choose the correct right on DPDT's application-process page, search the relevant public records and file through bd.wipo.net/efiling-dashboard or the route specified by DPDT.
notes: Use a trademark for a brand, a patent for a qualifying invention and an industrial design for a product's visual design. RJSC name clearance only checks the proposed entity name and does not provide trademark protection.

name: Copyright Office Bangladesh
service: Copyright registration for literary, dramatic, musical, artistic, film, sound-recording, broadcast and computer-software works.
process: Submit the category-specific application and supporting work through the Copyright Office's e-Copyright system and pay the published fee.
applicationPath: Create an account at bcoecopyright.gov.bd, choose the correct work category and follow the Copyright Office's document and fee instructions.
notes: Registration is not mandatory for copyright to exist, but the Copyright Office says its certificate can be used as evidence if ownership is disputed. For commissioned, employee-created or jointly owned work, establish who owns the rights before applying.

name: Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution (BSTI)
service: Bangladesh Standards, product testing and Certification Marks licences for products subject to compulsory or voluntary certification.
process: Follow the relevant Certification Marks process, including application, factory assessment and product sampling or testing against the applicable Bangladesh Standard.
applicationPath: Check BSTI's current mandatory-products list, identify the applicable standard, then follow the published CM licence issue or renewal steps and fee schedule.
notes: Manufacturers and importers should check the exact product against BSTI's compulsory-certification list before production or release. The applicable standard, samples, inspection steps and fees are product-specific; voluntary certification and testing are separate options.

name: Directorate General of Drug Administration (DGDA)
service: Licensing, product registration and regulatory oversight for drugs, cosmetics, vaccines, medical devices, pharmacies and pharmaceutical manufacturers.
process: Use the DGDA system assigned to the service, submit the product or establishment documents and complete any required review or premises inspection.
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
applicationPath: Start with DGDA's current notices and registered-product database, then use rims.dgda.gov.bd or the pharmacy application route for the specific licence or registration.
notes: A founder manufacturing, importing, distributing or selling a regulated health or cosmetics product may need approval for both the product and the establishment. Determine the product classification before launch; a trade licence alone is not market authorisation.

name: Fire Service and Civil Defence Directorate
service: Fire licence issue, reassessment and renewal for business and industrial premises.
process: Apply through the e-Fire Licence portal with the premises and business information; Fire Service reviews the submission and assesses the site's compliance.
applicationPath: Submit a new-licence or reassessment application at elicense.fireservice.gov.bd; use the renewal option when it is available for the relevant licence year.
notes: The fire licence addresses the safety of the operating premises, so the building use, layout and risk matter alongside the company details. Building NOC, fire-safety training, drills and risk assessments are related but separate Fire Service workflows.

name: Bangladesh Bank
service: Foreign-investment share issue and transfer reporting, temporary investment accounts, dividend and share-sale repatriation, portfolio-investment routes and other foreign-exchange transactions.
process: Most filings and remittances are handled through an authorised dealer bank under Bangladesh Bank rules; only specified cases require prior central-bank approval.
applicationPath: Engage an authorised dealer bank before money moves, use the FEID portal for current requirements and use BIDA OSS for a temporary non-resident account where applicable.
notes: Founders receiving foreign equity or repatriating investment proceeds should structure the transaction through formal banking channels and complete the required reporting on time. Many transactions operate under general permission, while larger or exceptional transfers may require valuation documents or Bangladesh Bank approval.
